To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BI-1 regulates Ca2+ homeoostasis in lymphoid cells and thereby controls cell function and survival.

BI-1 deficiency leads to a severe immune phenotype with leukopenia, erythrocytopenia, increased splenic marginal zone, higher cytosolic and Ca2+ levels in the ER and mitochondria, and increased NF-κB nuclear translocation, which results in spontaneous lymphocyte death in vitro, attenuated T- and B-cell-dependent experimental autoimmune disease in vivo and reduced antibody production.
BI-1 is essential for immune cell homeostasis, function and survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the ER in the regulation of intracellular Ca2+, protein folding and immune function.
the role of the Ca2+ channel BAX (Bcl-2 associated X protein) inhibitor 1 in the regulation of immune cells and its role in the pathophysiology of autoimmune diseases.
the role of Ca2+ in lymphocyte biology and its impact on immune function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BI-1 is an essential Ca2+ leak regulator in lymphocytes and that its absence results in an increased susceptibility to Ca2+-dependent cell death.
BI-1 deficiency leads to a failure of the adaptive immune response due to increased cytoplasmic Ca2+ levels in T cells and B cells.
BI-1 is a critical component in the Ca2+ signaling machinery in the immune system, thereby linking Ca2+ homeodynamics to the regulation of cell survival and death in immune cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

BI-1 is a crucial regulator for the adaptive immune response, as BI-1 deficiency leads to increased intracellular Ca2+, which in turn causes mitochondrial Ca2+ overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ultimately cell death.
BAX inhibitor-1 has an essential role in maintaining Ca2+ homeoostasis in lymphoid cells, and that this role is important for their function.
BI-1 is an ER Ca2+ leak-channel that is critical for lymphocyte function and survival, thereby providing a link between Ca2+ and protein-folding homeostasis in the ER.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BI-1 is a critical regulator of the adaptive immune response, which may have therapeutic implications for immune-mediated disorders.
BI-1 is a critical Ca2+ channel for the function of the adaptive immune cells.
Ca2+ homeodynamics in lymphocytes is crucial for immune cell homeostasis and survival, as well as for the proper functioning of the immune system.
